t: The length of a Valian Year
r: Annals of Aman: 1 V.Y. = 9.582 sun-years, with Tolkien's own arithmetic; NoME's late time-schemes: 1 V.Y. = 144 sun-years.
a: Never reconciled — both are the Professor's own, decades apart. The archive computes with 9.582 and flags the alternative on every pre-Sun date.
w: HoME X (AAm) vs NoME Pt I · shown in the timeline's epoch note

r: Earliest note (WoJ): a son of Finrod's house; published Silmarillion: son of Fingon (an editorial construction CT later regretted); latest manuscript (Shibboleth): son of Orodreth, himself moved to son of Angrod.
a: RULED 1 August 2026 by the archive's owner: THE FATHER IS ORODRETH, following the latest manuscript layer (HoME XII, The Shibboleth of Feanor), with the confusion recorded everywhere relevant. This entry is no longer a description of an open question — it is the record of a decided one, and of what was decided against. The latest manuscript layer is Orodreth; the published Silmarillion text is acknowledged editorial and is NOT corrected in arda_index, which reproduces Tolkien's own published index and reads 'Ereinion: Scion of Kings, the son of Fingon'. The archive records the disagreement rather than editing a source. The trees draw Orodreth at confidence M and display all three variants. The mother is a separate and still-open silence: PoME, in the Orodreth version, says only 'Their mother was a Sindarin lady of the North. She called her son Gil-galad' — see arda_silences, 'Who was Gil-galad's mother?'
w: WoJ; Silm; HoME XII · genealogy node gilgalad

t: Orodreth's own place in the House of Finarfin
r: Published Silm: son of Finarfin, brother of Finrod; Shibboleth: son of Angrod, Finrod's nephew.
a: Late manuscript (nephew) drawn, published variant noted.
w: Silm table I vs HoME XII · genealogy

r: Published Silm: survives to the Third Kinslaying; Shibboleth: burned with the ships at Losgar.

r: UT main scheme: Sindar of Doriath, grandson of Elmo; a late note: a Teleri of Aman (Galadriel's kinsman there).
a: UT's Sindarin descent drawn [I-M]; the Aman variant noted. Christopher Tolkien's own words on the whole Galadriel-and-Celeborn history: "There is no part of the history of Middle-earth more full of problems than the story of Galadriel and Celeborn, and it must be admitted that there are severe inconsistencies 'embedded in the traditions'."
w: UT, Hist. of Galadriel & Celeborn (opening paragraph) · genealogy

t: The history of Galadriel and Celeborn entire
r: UT presents several incompatible schemes of their Second-Age movements (Eregion, Lórinand, the sea-longing), explicitly declining to harmonize.
a: The archive uses only movements attested per-scheme with the scheme named; no composite invented.

r: Son of Amdír (UT's adopted line); a variant making him son of Galadriel and Celeborn is reported and rejected by CT.
UT prints two traditions side by side: Enerdhil of Gondolin, or Celebrimbor in Eregion (perhaps two stones).
a: Both shown as a fork on the artifact card; no verdict.

r: UT gives three fates side by side — they remained in the East, or perished, or were ensnared by Sauron and became his servants. PoME gives a fourth and opposite account, naming them Morinehtar and Rómestámo, 'Darkness-slayer and East-helper', arriving in the SECOND Age and having 'very great influence… in weakening and disarraying the forces of East'.
a: Both accounts stated wherever the Istari appear; the later note is later. Tolkien also wrote in 1956 that their names did not exist; a NoME scheme adds Palacendo and Haimenar as Guardians of Cuiviénen. Four accounts, not two. The article is absent on purpose: PoME t1_12:12746 reads 'forces of East'. 'forces of the East' does occur, in Unfinished Tales, but of a different passage -- a string match is not a citation. The Loremaster protected the identical insertion in arda_silences.json the same way at d50a311.
w: The PoME account is the latest and the most favourable; UT offers its three as alternatives, not as ignorance.

r: The Etymologies' Beleriandic branch is 'Noldorin' (the Exiles' own tongue); the post-LotR re-conception makes Beleriand's tongue Sindarin, adopted by the Noldor.

t: Tar-Ardamin in the line of kings
r: UT's Line of Elros includes Tar-Ardamin (Ar-Abattârik); App A's list omits him, making Ar-Adûnakhôr son of Tar-Calmacil. Christopher Tolkien does not hedge about which is right: "it now seems perfectly clear, from the fact alone that Tar-Ardamin's death-date is here given as 2899, that he was omitted in error from the list in The Lord of the Rings".
a: UT's fuller line drawn; App A's omission flagged on the node. Not a standing tension so much as a published error the author's editor identified — the archive follows his verdict, and records that he reached one.
w: UT vs LotR App A · genealogy

r: Corrupted Elves (published Silm's frame); corrupted Men, beast-forms, and Maiar-led automata are all weighed in Myths Transformed — Tolkien never settled it.
a: The peoples taxonomy draws the descent-link dashed with the divergence stated.
w: Silm 3 vs HoME X, Myths Transformed · peoples taxonomy

t: Map against text: Angband to Menegroth
r: The Annals of Beleriand say the gates of Morgoth were 'but one hundred and fifty leagues distant from the bridge of Menegroth; far and yet all too near' — quoted by Christopher Tolkien in his introduction to The Children of Húrin, where he uses the figure and does not remark on the map. Tolkien's own map scale gives roughly 73 leagues, under half of it.
a: The archive keeps map-consistent geometry and flags the textual figure. Christopher Tolkien's own response to the same tension is recorded rather than smoothed: he left Thangorodrim off the published map. A map-text tension he declined to resolve, not one nobody noticed.
w: Annals of Beleriand (quoted at CoH intro) vs the published Silm map · RECONSTRUCTION.md B2, §3.1

t: Myths Transformed: the Sun and Moon
r: The published cosmology (fruit and flower of the Trees) against the late astronomical re-conception where Sun and Moon precede the Trees' end.
a: The archive's chronology uses the published frame (the corpus's own narrative spine) and records the late alternative here.
w: Silm 11 vs HoME X · timeline epoch note

cls: not a contradiction — reconciled in the source
t: The éored's arithmetic does not bend
r: UT n.36 gives the definition and the exception IN THE SAME NOTE, in Tolkien's own words: a full éored is 'not less than 120 men' and a hundredth of the Full Muster, but 'no such host, of course, had ever ridden all together to war beyond the Mark', and 'owing to losses in the western war, the hastiness of the Muster, and the threat from North and East, Théoden only led out a host of some six thousand spears'. The note also confirms Éomer's éored at exactly 120 (105 counted by Legolas, 15 lost).
a: The armies model uses both numbers, which is right — but they were never in conflict, so this is no longer registered as an unreconciled tension. Kept, not deleted, because the pairing is worth showing: it is the source explaining itself.
w: UT n.36 (quoted in full there) · ARMIES.md
